scenes.purpose: Name the product and say what it does.
scenes.audience_benefit: Viewer knows what OI is before any interface appears.
scenes.narration: Opening Intelligence, or OI, helps you identify commercial door hardware and organize the information about each opening—from the products installed to the service work performed.

Cross-dissolve to a still photograph of a commercial door opening; hold to the end of the line.
scenes.expected_visible_result: Viewer sees the product name and a real commercial opening before any UI appears.

scenes.title: Preview the walkthrough
scenes.purpose: Promise the walkthrough, showing the actual screens named.
scenes.audience_benefit: Viewer knows the scope and can decide to keep watching.
scenes.narration: Let me show you how it works. We'll walk through three different openings, photograph the hardware and see what OI can support from those photographs, review the manufacturer's documentation, and save each part. We'll also record the door and frame details for those same openings. For each opening, we'll finish the opening before looking at what purchasing receives. After all three, we'll log a service call and see how the information helps the facility team.
screen_action: Three short readable previews, ~4s each, of screens named in the line: (1) the identification result card, (2) the Cal-Royal CR441 cut sheet, (3) the Door & frame spec panel.
No SKU card and no purchasing screen in this preview (reserved for CH8).
scenes.expected_visible_result: Viewer sees the actual screens promised, at readable size.
required_source_assets: prototype/build/index.html (the controlled demonstration build — recorded live, no external asset)
scenes.blocked_reason: Needs in-app previews of the cut sheet and the door & frame panel — so it follows the local demonstration mode and PC-3, not a credentials question.
scenes.change_note: v1.1: the preview now promises what OI can support from the photographs rather than a flat 'identify the hardware', so the introduction cannot over-promise a model-level result.

scenes.title: What an uncertain result carries
scenes.purpose: Show that unresolved identifications are routed for human review and feed future recognition performance.
scenes.audience_benefit: Facilities see that uncertainty is tracked rather than buried; manufacturers see how representation improves over time.
scenes.narration: When a part stays uncertain, that's kept rather than smoothed over. The saved record carries what OI predicted, how confident it was at each level, what evidence it asked for, and anything I entered for calibration. The accuracy panel reports how those calls are tracking—identification accuracy, confidence calibration, and recent scans.
screen_action: Open the 'Testing — identification accuracy' panel; hold on the loaded figures.
Show the saved record for the uncertain part and its Needs Review status.
Show only the record and the accuracy panel.
scenes.expected_visible_result: The Needs Review status on the saved record, and the accuracy panel with real loaded figures.
acceptance_criteria: Nothing states or implies that a visible review queue exists in the Field App. There is none.
Only the Needs Review status, the saved-record fields and the accuracy panel are shown.
Any figure shown is one the application actually loaded.

The demonstration label must be visible on screen wherever an accuracy figure is: "Demonstration data — illustrates metric calculation; not measured field performance." — rendered above the figures, in the same frame, for the whole time any figure is shown.
No figure from this dataset may be described as measured field accuracy or as evidence of six-month field performance. It illustrates how the metric is calculated, nothing more.
The narration covers the SEPARATION — OI recognition, technician assistance, final record completion — and does not present any percentage as a product-performance claim.
scenes.caption: What the saved record carries
scenes.change_note: v1.1g: demonstration label required on every accuracy figure; no percentage may be presented as a product-performance claim. Narration unchanged.

scenes.title: Calibration, and where improvement comes from
scenes.purpose: Show that technician-entered true models sit beside predictions and feed the accuracy measures.
scenes.audience_benefit: Everyone sees the mechanism by which recognition is meant to get better, stated as intent rather than as a delivered result.
scenes.narration: Every model a technician enters puts a known answer beside a prediction. That pairing is what the accuracy figures are built from—how often the call was right, and how well the confidence matched the outcome. What you're looking at is the measurement. Improving recognition is the work it feeds, and it's measured here rather than claimed.
screen_action: Open the accuracy view; hold on each heading with its real loaded values.
scenes.expected_visible_result: The accuracy views load with real values.
acceptance_criteria: The improvement loop is stated as intent and as measurement — never as a demonstrated improvement.
Only figures the application actually loads are shown.
Nothing presents demonstration-image results as measured field accuracy. The six-month field-trial positioning is maintained.

The demonstration label must be visible on screen wherever an accuracy figure is: "Demonstration data — illustrates metric calculation; not measured field performance." — rendered above the figures, in the same frame, for the whole time any figure is shown.
No figure from this dataset may be described as measured field accuracy or as evidence of six-month field performance. It illustrates how the metric is calculated, nothing more.
The narration covers the SEPARATION — OI recognition, technician assistance, final record completion — and does not present any percentage as a product-performance claim.
scenes.caption: Measured, not claimed
scenes.change_note: v1.1g: demonstration label required on every accuracy figure; no percentage may be presented as a product-performance claim. Narration unchanged.
